objective: 请对当前 Quant 系统进行一次**从真实可运行闭环出发的全面审查、重构、验证与持续优化**，最终目标不是增加更多模块、策略、Agent 或“自我进化”概念，而是建立一个能够在严格风险约束下，从真实市场数据出发，完成 **observe → understand → generate decision → risk check → execute → broker fill → reconcile → PnL attribution → counterfactual evaluation → reflection → hypothesis → candidate strategy/model → offline validation → shadow/probation → live validation → promote/scale/pause/retire → repeat** 的完整自动闭环，并最终用长期、prospective、after-cost、risk-adjusted live net PnL 判断系统是否真正产生价值。第一步不要继续开发新功能，而是从代码、配置、数据库、journal、strategy registry、模型、文档和实际运行路径出发，对整个 repository 做一次事实级审查：明确每一个已经设计、实现或文档中声明的组件到底是否被真实调用、是否影响生产决策、是否有数据输入输出、是否存在只写了但从未使用的 dead code / unused feature / unused strategy / unused model / unused reflection / unused lifecycle / unused risk rule / duplicated abstraction / wrapper / historical path，并将所有能力分类为 **actively used / partially wired / implemented but unused / obsolete / duplicated / broken / missing**；特别检查“看起来已经有”但实际上没有进入真实交易闭环的功能，禁止把配置存在、函数存在、测试存在或文档存在等同于功能真正有效。随后以**最小可靠闭环优先**为原则进行重构，严格执行 **delete → merge → simplify → reuse → repair → only then add**：先删除或隔离无效和重复路径，统一唯一的数据流、控制流、状态来源、PnL ledger、strategy lifecycle、experiment registry、execution truth 和运行入口，确保主系统能够稳定完成一轮真实 end-to-end cycle，并为每一步建立明确输入、输出、责任边界、失败行为、日志、provenance 和自动测试。优先补齐当前真正决定系统能否学习的基础设施，包括完整 fill/trade/position/strategy/model attribution、realized/unrealized/net PnL、fees/slippage/cost accounting、BUY/SELL/HOLD counterfactual ledger、market/regime context、strategy lineage、experiment ledger、失败实验记录、模型预测与实际结果对齐，以及 lifecycle 的显式 state-machine invariants；任何 promotion、mutation 或自主修改都必须基于这些可验证证据，而不是 LLM 主观总结。将生产系统与研究/进化系统彻底分离：生产层只负责 data → decision → allocation → immutable Guardian → execution → reconciliation，学习层负责 diagnosis → hypothesis → candidate generation → backtest → walk-forward OOS → robustness → multiple-testing/overfitting control → shadow → small-capital probation → promotion/retirement；LLM 可以用于 reasoning、failure diagnosis、hypothesis generation、strategy proposal 和 research orchestration，但不得直接修改 Guardian、global risk limits、broker credentials、kill switch、audit rules 或未经验证直接修改 production behavior。不要把“交易次数更多”“HOLD rate 更低”“策略数量更多”“LLM 自己改代码”作为成功标准；先解释每一次 decision 是否正确，特别是对 HOLD 计算未来 counterfactual outcome，区分 good hold、missed alpha、avoided loss 和 false trade。对所有已有 strategy/model 建立 champion–challenger 和统一 StrategySpec，自动检测 semantic/behavioral duplicate，阻止 strategy zoo 无限制膨胀；新 candidate 必须说明它解决了什么已经观察到的 failure、与已有策略有什么本质区别、用了什么数据、经过了多少次搜索，并记录所有失败 trial，避免自动 data mining 和 selection bias。整个优化过程必须遵循“**先跑通闭环，再提高正确性，再提高研究能力，再增加自主性，最后才扩大资金**”的顺序：Phase 0 先做到 syntax/import/tests/service startup/restart/recovery/broker reconciliation 全部 PASS；Phase 1 完成真实交易和 PnL attribution；Phase 2 完成 counterfactual 与 decision-quality evaluation；Phase 3 建立 strategy/model/experiment registry；Phase 4 建立严格 offline backtest、walk-forward、cost、leakage、stress 和 overfitting validation；Phase 5 完成 shadow trading；Phase 6 才允许 evidence-gated probation；Phase 7 根据 prospective live evidence 自动 promote/pause/retire；Phase 8 再加入 regime-aware portfolio allocation、model retraining 和 strategy evolution；只有前一阶段 exit criteria 全部满足才能进入下一阶段。每次修改后都必须运行统一的 `make verify` 或等价命令，至少验证 software、syntax/import、unit/integration、data integrity、point-in-time/no-leakage、PnL accounting、lifecycle invariants、Guardian bypass prevention、replay determinism、crash recovery、broker reconciliation、shadow/live consistency，并要求 `FAIL=0`；任何失败不能被 warning 或 fallback 掩盖。最终请输出并持续维护一份事实级系统文档，明确：① 当前真实运行架构和唯一 end-to-end data/control flow；② 所有组件的 used/unused/broken/missing 审查表；③ 当前闭环在哪里真正断裂；④ 哪些模块应该删除、合并、修复或保留；⑤ 每个阶段的具体实现任务、依赖关系、测试方法、exit criteria 和验证结果；⑥ 当前赚钱或亏钱到底由 signal、model、strategy、allocation、execution、cost 还是 regime 导致；⑦ 当前系统哪些能力已经有证据证明，哪些只是设计目标；⑧ 下一轮只选择对“真实 after-cost risk-adjusted live profitability”最有价值的 1–3 个改动执行。整个项目的最高原则是：**不要优化一个尚未闭环的系统，不要让无法归因的结果驱动学习，不要让未经验证的学习结果进入生产，不要用复杂度代替能力；先让每一条数据、每一个决策、每一个订单、每一美元 PnL 和每一次策略变化都可以追踪、解释、复现和验证，再逐步让系统自动学习和自动进化。最终唯一有效的外部成功标准是：在固定风险边界和真实交易成本下，系统能否持续产生可复现、可归因、经样本外和 prospective live trading 验证的正净收益，而不是回测数字、策略数量或自治程度本身。**

progressNotes.summary: Regime context implemented, completing the measurement half of objective deliverable 6. regime.py derives the regime from the realized price series (only one last_price per cycle exists - no OHLC, volume or VIX), and deliberately does NOT allocate by regime since allocation is Phase 8 and starting it before earlier phases finish would be entering a phase out of order. The limitation is stated rather than buried: these are last-trade prints on a 5-minute cycle, not exchange bars, so volatility is noisier and slightly inflated by intra-interval moves, and a gap between samples reads as a move that may have occurred anywhere within it. The live result is mostly "cannot tell": of 467 bars, 391 are UNKNOWN and 76 TRENDING_DOWN, and only 78 bars have a contiguous window at all - the current regime cannot be labelled because the last 78 bars span a gap over 30 minutes. A window spanning a gap is refused rather than classified, because the journal contains a 97-day outage and a "recent volatility" across it would describe two different months as one market. The consequence is the honest one: every one of the 23 profitable lots was opened in a window that cannot be labelled, so the regime row is no longer CANNOT ATTRIBUTE because code was missing but because it was MEASURED and came back unusable - the loop now knows it cannot answer this rather than not knowing that it could not. The unmeasurable bucket is reported rather than dropped, since a bucket that silently vanishes is how a conclusion gets drawn from the measurable minority. Two properties enforced rather than assumed: point-in-time (a label at bar i uses bars up to i only, with the test that matters being that appending future bars cannot change an earlier label - a regime label on a past decision is exactly the context that leaks, and it leaks silently), and volatility overriding direction (a steep decline is UNSTABLE not TRENDING_DOWN, because filing a violent decline as a calm downtrend understates the risk of trading through it). A test caught my own fixture making that mistake - a -2.0-per-bar series expected to be TRENDING_DOWN, and the classifier was right while the test was wrong - and the same test showed the classifier describes the window it is given, so with the default 78-bar window a series that rose then fell is TRENDING_UP because the rise dominates, which is correct and is now tested with a 30-bar window rather than expecting the classifier to see through its own window. Commit 8a115a8. make verify: 21 classes, 0 failed, 614 distinct tests, 91/91 audit, doctor OK, exit 0.
progressNotes.next: Objective deliverable 6 is now complete: all seven causes are reported, and regime is the last one that was purely absent - it is now measured and its unusability on this data is a finding. Remaining doc deliverables are 5 (per-phase implementation tasks, dependencies, test methods, exit criteria and verification results), 7 (proven capability vs design target) and 8 (the next 1-3 highest-value changes). Also open: unrealized PnL (only realized is attributed, so open lots contribute nothing to the account picture) and the Phase 3 model-registry gap. Given three findings now point the same way - the model has contributed 0.00 to PnL, all 67 LLM decisions are unscoreable because the market has been closed, and only 78 of 467 bars have a contiguous window so regime cannot be labelled - the data-sparseness itself is arguably the binding constraint on everything downstream, and a doc deliverable recording that honestly may be more valuable than further instrumentation. Phase 7 and the calibration verdict both need market hours.

Quantified the binding constraint and delivered objective deliverables 5, 7 and 8 as docs/superpowers/PHASES.md. Quantifying first, because three separate findings turned out to have one cause: the model contributing 0.00, all 67 llm decisions being unscoreable, and only 78 of 467 bars having a contiguous window. 467 distinct observations across 111.4 days on 10 distinct trading days (9% of elapsed days), mean interval 344 min against a configured 300 s, max gap 140841 min (97.8 days). But the median gap is exactly 5 min, matching daemon_interval_seconds, and on the days it ran coverage was a full session with the most recent day at 1-minute granularity - so the sampling rate is correct and the daemon simply did not run. This is not a configuration defect and there is nothing to fix in the code: ten trading days cannot support an out-of-sample claim, a calibration verdict or a regime attribution, and every instrument built this session now says so rather than guessing. The systemd blocker was re-tested rather than repeated: df -h ~ reports 1.8T free on /home which looks like there is no problem and is misleading, because df shows the filesystem while the limit that bites is a per-user quota - mkdir ~/.config/systemd still fails with "Disk quota exceeded". $HOME holds 11G, of which .cache is 835M and .local is 707M; freeing either would let minictrl install-service write a permanent unit. That is the third time this session a plausible-looking signal turned out to be the wrong one - df, a grep for "backtest" matching a docstring, and a doctor check printing a stale claim. Also found a contradiction in STATUS.md by checking my own edit rather than trusting it: a pointer edit created two lines that contradicted each other and left a withdrawn claim standing three lines below ("shadow is implemented" alongside "shadow is merged into probation, not missing"). Both earlier notes are now recorded as withdrawn with the reason, because a withdrawn claim left standing is worse than one never made. That edit also silently did nothing on its first attempt because it targeted a line that no longer existed - the same "looks applied but isn't" shape this audit has been removing all session, this time in my own tooling. PHASES.md records: per-phase tasks/dependencies/test methods/exit criteria/verification results (Phase 3 marked PARTIAL for a missing component rather than thin data - no model registry, since TradeDecision has no model field so the 67 llm decisions cannot be separated by prompt or model version); proven-vs-design-target; the full 7-cause PnL attribution; and the next three changes chosen by what unblocks the most - run and let evidence accumulate with the systemd fix protecting it, close the Phase 3 model-registry gap, and unrealized PnL. Phase 8 is explicitly not next. Commit 70dccbf. make verify: 21 classes, 0 failed, 614 distinct tests, 91/91 audit, doctor OK, exit 0.
progressNotes.next: All seven explicit doc deliverables are now covered: 1 architecture/flow and 2-4 component classification in SYSTEM_AUDIT.md, 5 phases and 7 proven-vs-target and 8 next changes in PHASES.md, 6 PnL cause attribution. The highest-value remaining work per deliverable 8 is the one item that is not a code change: run and let evidence accumulate, protected by making the systemd units reboot-persistent. That requires freeing $HOME quota (.cache 835M or .local 707M) so minictrl install-service can write a permanent unit, or setting MIN_AGENT_UNIT_DIR to a path the user manager reads. Second is the Phase 3 model registry (TradeDecision has no model field, so the 67 llm decisions cannot be attributed to a prompt or model version). Third is unrealized PnL. Phase 7 and the calibration verdict both need market hours. The quota fix is arguably a user action since it means deleting cache directories under $HOME, and the daemon's continued unattended operation is the other thing only the user can confirm.

Closed the Phase 3 gap - the only phase that was partial for a missing component rather than thin data. Every decision recorded decision_source (llm, fallback_policy_engine, baseline) but not WHICH model, so the 67 llm decisions could not be separated by prompt or model version and no outcome could ever be attributed to a model change. The model was upgraded during this project (Ollama 0.34.4, qwen3.8:27b, single-CUDA pin) and without provenance that upgrade is invisible in the record and its effect is unmeasurable forever. TradeDecision.model now records it, stamped AT THE POINT THE MODEL IS CALLED rather than inferred from config later - the model can be swapped between the call and the journal write, and a decision attributed to the wrong version is worse than one with no attribution. A model named inside the response itself wins over the configured name because that is the one that actually served the request, and the fallback path names itself fallback_policy_engine so a fallback decision can never be counted as a model's work. model_registry.py is a view over the journal like the experiment registry and lineage, with a test asserting it exposes no save/write/append, because a persisted store of model performance would be a second source of truth about numbers already recorded and would drift. The history is NOT back-filled: all 920 cycles predate the field and report UNATTRIBUTED, since assigning them the currently configured model would assert a fact about the past that is not known and would make every future comparison look like evidence for a model that never ran. The doctor check is a warning while that is true - correct rather than noisy - and clears itself as soon as the market is open and new decisions are stamped. PHASES.md updated so Phase 3 reads MET and deliverable 8 no longer lists the registry as pending. Implemented unrealized PnL - the last code item from deliverable 8. Only realized PnL was attributed, so a position the agent was holding contributed nothing to its own record and the account figure and the agent figure could never be reconciled even in principle: one measured closed trades, the other measured everything, and the gap could only be explained away. PnLEvidence now carries open_lots, unrealized_pnl, net_pnl and net_of_fees, with open lots keeping the strategy that opened them to match the realized side's rule (the strategy that opens a lot is the one expected to realize its PnL, which may not be the strategy that eventually sells it). Verified by the daemon writing it rather than by a script: realized 564.39, open lots empty, unrealized 0.0, net 564.39, net of fees 564.39 - the agent holds no SPY (account positions are BIL, TLT, XLB, XLE, XLF) so unrealized is 0 and net equals realized, which is the correct answer and not a stub, and the machinery is proven only by test against a live position because there is no live position. The refusal that matters: an open lot whose price is unknown is reported with current_price None and unrealized_pnl None, never valued at its entry price, because marking a position at its own cost reports it as worth exactly nothing - a fabricated number wearing the appearance of a measurement. This surfaced a real finding now visible in doctor: 29 shares were sold under trend-follow-sell-002 that no linked BUY can account for. The account holds no SPY so those shares came from somewhere the fill linkage cannot see - a pre-existing position, a fill whose client_order_id never linked, or a lot opened before the journal began. The 23 closed lots carrying the +564.39 are all fully linked so the verified figure is unaffected, but 29 shares of unexplained selling belongs in a health report rather than a payload field. It is explicitly NOT diagnosed: it needs the ORDER_FILL_CONFIRMED events for that strategy traced back, which is real work and not something to guess at. A test also caught the doctor implementation formatting unrealized unconditionally, which would have raised TypeError on its own history since every stored PNL event predates the field - the same shape as reading a JournalEvent as a dict; it now degrades to net alone. Diagnosed the 29 unmatched shares and found the most serious defect in the project. Traced back: the agent bought 23 shares, the account held 52, and a single SELL of 52 was approved and filled - liquidating 29 shares, 56%, of a pre-existing SPY position belonging to the account owner. The check that existed was necessary but not sufficient: "cannot sell more than known holdings" used the ACCOUNT's holdings, and the account did hold 52. It bounded selling to the account's book - the owner's book plus the agent's - and said nothing about which of those the agent had any right to sell. This is an asymmetry in my own earlier fix: bounding max_total_exposure to the allowlist was justified as "the agent can only increase exposure by buying allowlist symbols, so bounding the allowlist book bounds everything it is able to do." True for increasing, plainly false for decreasing - the agent can reduce the owner's position without limit by selling shares it never bought. Worse, the scoping change made that path MORE reachable, because a symbol the agent had never traded was previously not in its book at all. Everything the reasoning predicted held, which is what makes a one-directional error so hard to notice. Fixed: a SELL is now bounded by what the agent holds, computed in the loop from ORDER_FILL_CONFIRMED events rather than from the account snapshot (the account snapshot being exactly the number that let this happen). When the agent's holding is unknown - no journal, unreadable journal - the SELL is REFUSED, and that direction is deliberate: a missed exit is recoverable since the next cycle retries and the position is unchanged, whereas liquidating someone's position is not. An unreadable journal is recorded in loop._agent_holding_errors rather than swallowed, because a silent None is indistinguishable from a legitimate "the agent holds nothing" - exactly the reading that allowed this. BUY is untouched: a probe with no holding yet is the normal case and refusing it would stop the agent ever opening anything. Four existing Guardian tests encoded the old contract, calling review() for a SELL without the agent's holding and asserting approval; they were correct when written and are updated, with new tests pinning both the refusal and the fact that a SELL within the agent's own holding is still permitted, because blocking every exit would be its own kind of danger. Started the requirement-by-requirement audit and immediately found a real gap: the objective's success criterion is AFTER-COST net PnL, and cost existed in the research backtest but was completely absent from the live ledger - a grep for commission/slippage/cost_pct in evaluator.py returned nothing, and all 23 lots recorded 0.00 buy and sell fees. So the number the system reported as its result was gross, and on paper the broker charges nothing, so nothing in the data would ever have revealed it. The backtest cost model and the counterfactual cost assumption both existed and both looked like cost accounting; the live PnL simply had none. Now observed and assumed are separate fields: net_of_fees and net_after_assumed_cost sit side by side, because on paper the observed fee is 0.00 and a number called "net" that silently means "gross, because the broker is free" is a label that outlives its assumption. Cost is charged on the notional actually traded, both sides, attributed to the strategy that opened the lot - the same rule the realized side uses. Live result: observed fees 0.00, assumed 0.05% round-trip = 8.67, taking +564.39 gross to +555.72 after cost - 1.5% of the gain, small but not zero, and the criterion is written on the after-cost number, so doctor now leads with it. Closed the second open audit requirement: failed-experiment records. The objective requires every failed trial to be recorded, because selection bias is invisible otherwise - keep the best of forty variants and report it as the only candidate and the number inherits the selection without showing it. Admission rejections were already recorded in production, but a backtest that failed its out-of-sample bar left NO trace at all: research/ wrote nothing, so a search could run, could fail, and leave behind no evidence it had happened. The obvious fix - letting research append to the production journal - would break the separation the objective also requires, for a good reason: a backtest that graded itself could then influence production state. So trials.py is a separate append-only sink in its own file that nothing in production reads, satisfying both requirements rather than trading one for the other. Writes are atomic with fsync; a write failure is reported by return value rather than raised into the caller, because the trial already ran and its value is in the result rather than the bookkeeping; a torn final line is skipped on read rather than costing the history behind it. Recorded live: 27 trials, 0 passed, 27 failed, all INSUFFICIENT. Three of my own mistakes, each caught by something rather than by reading the diff: the first trial payload keyed on the whole verdict sentence, so two identical outcomes landed in different buckets because their trade counts differed - defeating the only thing the grouping is for, so the verdict is now split into a code and a detail; the call site for the doctor check was missing because the insertion anchor did not match, and the doctor-checks-reachable gate caught it immediately, the second time that gate has caught a check that was defined, wired and dead; and the production-research-separation gate caught a real violation I had just introduced - I put the trial-ledger check in doctor, so production imported the research layer it is meant to be independent of. Found and fixed the most operationally serious remaining defect, by watching rather than reading. The market opened at 09:30, the loop produced one cycle at 09:30:00, then nothing for 11 minutes against a configured 5-minute interval. The heartbeat said RUNNING and the model answered a trivial prompt in 1.6s, so neither a crash nor a slow model explained it. MarketScheduler.sleep_seconds computed its target as seconds_until_next_close while the market was open, capped by max_sleep. Verified against the real broker clock: market_is_open True, configured interval 300s, actual cadence 900s, because max_sleep is maintenance_interval_seconds. The daemon was taking one cycle every 15 minutes during a session instead of every 5, and daemon_interval_seconds did nothing exactly when it mattered. Nothing reported it: heartbeat fresh, process alive, make verify green - the only symptom was that the market opened, produced a single cycle, and went quiet. That is the objective's "configuration existing is not the capability working" in its purest form, and the cost was three times fewer decisions per session plus a directly slower accumulation of the 69 unscoreable decisions everything depends on. Fixed: while open the loop sleeps min(default_interval, max_sleep); while closed it sleeps until the next open, capped, so maintenance still runs overnight. Confirmed working: second cycle at 09:47:17, heartbeat fresh at 132s, both cycles provenance-stamped. A test had encoded the defect - test_scheduler_caps_sleep_at_max_sleep asserted the loop would sleep 60s against a configured 30 while the market was open. Rewritten to the contract with the shipped 300/900 numbers pinned so it cannot regress silently; same pattern as the four SELL tests, since a test is not automatically right and "the test says so" is not "the behaviour is right". progressNotes.summary: Operator instruction: use only qwen3.8:27b, not two models, and make it as fast as possible. Chasing that surfaced two claims of mine that were plain wrong earlier today, which is the substance of this checkpoint. First: the model WAS on the GPU the whole time. I had reported it was "not running on the GPU at all" from zero nvidia-smi utilisation. Startup logs show all 37 layers offloaded to GPU-0d16a3ed (CUDA, compute 7.5, Quadro RTX 8000) with flash attention on, and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 working correctly. The zero utilisation was an idle GPU - the model had been unloaded when the 30m keep-alive expired with the market closed. Grepping the ollama binary for CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES returns nothing because it is honoured in the CUDA layer, not by ollama's parser; absence of the string was not evidence. Second: the 120s timeouts were cold-load, not slow inference. Warm, a real decision takes 10-24s; unloaded, the call must first read 16.33 GiB of weights off /localscratch, about three minutes, against a 120s timeout - which is exactly the signature of the recorded off-hours CURRICULUM_FAILED timeouts. Config: MAX_LOADED_MODELS 2->1 (the agent pins one model and a second slot let another evict it; two 27B-class models do not fit in 45 GiB beside KV cache), KEEP_ALIVE 30m->-1 (one model on a dedicated card should not unload), num_ctx 32768->4096 (KV cache is allocated for the full window even when unused). Measured 52.2s -> 19.5s on a real context, 17.8s -> 4.6s on the shortest. num_ctx=4096 is safe by measurement, not taste: largest real context ~253 tokens in, longest measured answer 814, so 3.5x headroom; 2048 would fit today and truncate the first context that grows a few open orders, which is a correctness bug dressed as a speedup. num_predict capping was tried and is a trap: at 160 tokens the response is empty with done_reason=length because the thinking block consumes the budget. /no_think was deliberately NOT adopted - it halves latency (23.2s -> 12.7s, same action) but changed confidence 0.72 -> 0.55 on a near-daily-limit context, and suppressing a hybrid model's reasoning to save wall-clock is a decision-quality change dressed as an infrastructure change. Most serious find: the units were installed where systemd never looks, which invalidates two of my own earlier claims from this same session. minictrl wrote to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, but the systemd user manager resolves unit paths from its own start-time environment, which has no XDG_CONFIG_HOME (show-environment returns only HOME), so it searched $HOME/.config/systemd/user and the tmpfs runtime dir. The files minictrl wrote were never opened by systemd; FragmentPath was the /run/user/29424 tmpfs copy; is-enabled reported "enabled" while the symlink pointed into tmpfs, so a reboot would have left dangling links and the units would never have returned; and the ollama edits had no effect on the running process, which is why the first restart appeared to do nothing. So my earlier claim that "the quota was never the blocker" was wrong - it was blocking the only durable location - and "survives a reboot" was wrong too. systemd_unit_dir.sh now asks the manager instead of trusting the shell, and refuses tmpfs unless MIN_AGENT_ALLOW_RUNTIME_UNITS=1. Units now install to $HOME/.config/systemd/user, FragmentPath points there, all three enablement links are durable, zero links into /run. This reintroduces a few KB of $HOME, which is unavoidable for a reboot-persistent user unit when the manager has no XDG_CONFIG_HOME; the repo remains the source of truth. Both bugs were invisible - a unit systemd cannot find still reports "enabled" - so both are now gates: units-where-systemd-looks plus self-test conditions 7 and 8 proving they go red, and four llm_decision tests pinning num_ctx and its headroom, including one that walks every /api/generate call site, which is how the curriculum transport in cli.py was found still on the server default. That test's first version flagged its own comment and its second walked back a fixed line count, so both are structural now. make verify: 24 classes, 0 failed, 1031 test executions, 91/91 audit, doctor OK, exit 0.
